description: Modeling bounds and abstractions: each states its bound, why the bounded property is safe, and how to lift it.
modeled_scope: Five paths in two roots, three content hashes, and small mtime/len values; intake lanes are collapsed onto one set; each worker step is atomic; direct API writes that bypass the intake (ApiRemove, ApiMove, ApiAssignDirMove, AppSidecarEdit, RotateImage, ExternalRenameDir) are synchronous, while ApiUpload stores the file and fire-and-forget enqueues intake; crashes occur between completed durable writes, the request phase is crash-free, and the drain admits one budgeted fault per attempt that reboots into the request phase; directory paths are flat fixed pairs. Not modeled: watcher delivery, general liveness, partial durable writes, and hierarchical directory paths. Sweep is split into enumerate + per-candidate re-check/apply, with batches accumulating across roots; move lease window is visible.

scopes.title: Initial converged state
scopes.bound: Every run starts from the fully matching initial state (init and the initial* record helpers in utils/quint/pipeline/merged.qnt).
scopes.why_safe: Convergence is about healing divergence, so runs introduce divergence explicitly before asserting the heal.
scopes.lifting: Start runs from arbitrary states (not yet modeled).

scopes.title: Finite bounds
scopes.bound: Five paths, three content hashes, three small mtime/len values (PATHS, HASHES, SMALL in utils/quint/pipeline/merged.qnt).
scopes.why_safe: The properties checked (identity match, no lost intake, no permanent staleness) are per-path and pairwise; bounds are sized to exhibit every guard outcome (match, mismatch, superseded, stale, missing) and to hold one two-asset subtree move plus a second sweep root.
scopes.lifting: Bound-escalation runs at larger sizes (not yet modeled).

scopes.title: Collapsed intake lanes
scopes.bound: The five intake lanes ride one intake set; priority scheduling is not modeled (see the intake comment in utils/quint/pipeline/merged.qnt).
scopes.why_safe: No checked property depends on lane order — guards are per-item (generation, snapshot), never positional.
scopes.lifting: Lane-aware scheduling with fairness properties (explicitly out of scope; Apalache/TLC stay out as well).

scopes.title: Atomic worker step
scopes.bound: Each worker action (WorkerApply*, skips, removes) applies in one step; there are no open/hash/apply micro-stages, so no modify-during-pipeline interleaving exists in the model.
scopes.why_safe: The hash-to-skip re-stat window is the only guarded window in code; the open-to-hash window is unguarded there too — the model matches the implementation's actual guarantee, not a stronger one.

scopes.title: Synchronous direct writes
scopes.bound: Actions that write the projection without the intake (ApiRemove, ApiMove, ApiAssignDirMove, AppSidecarEdit, ExternalRenameDir) apply in the same step as their filesystem effect, with no serial write queue (tasks/queue/writer.rs) inbox (see the direct-write comment in utils/quint/pipeline/merged.qnt). RotateWriteSidecar/RotateFinish are the two-phase rotate window (SCOPE-10). ApiUpload is excluded: it stores the file and fire-and-forget enqueues intake (submit_uploaded_path -> submit_watcher_index), so the projection write happens later in tasks/queue/worker.rs intake application.
scopes.why_safe: The model proves convergence given synchronous writes; the lag between acknowledgment and visibility is a known divergence, tracked as an open fault rather than assumed away. ApiUpload no longer writes the projection synchronously, so its visibility lag is the by-design unindexed window (N8) rather than a barrier fault.
scopes.lifting: A writerInbox pending state mirroring the serial writer.

scopes.title: Completed-write crash abstraction
scopes.bound: Crash and DB-loss actions occur between completed durable writes: the model never represents a partially written row or sidecar (PROCESS_CRASH drops volatile intake; DB_LOSS clears the row map; DERIVED_STORE_LOSS clears thumbnail flags).
scopes.why_safe: The recovery runs assert convergence from every interrupted state the model represents (queue lost, rows cleared, thumbnails lost, sidecar ahead of row), so the proof does not lean on partial-write behaviour; store transaction durability is a property of redb, outside this model.
scopes.lifting: Model partial durable writes and store transactions explicitly.

scopes.title: Flat directory paths
scopes.bound: Path IDs carry no directory hierarchy. A directory rename is a fixed finite set of path pairs (SUBTREE_PAIRS in utils/quint/pipeline/merged.qnt) moved atomically; arbitrary subtrees are not modeled.
scopes.why_safe: The property under proof is per-descendant row/path consistency plus all-or-nothing row updates, which a fixed two-asset pair set exhibits at the model's bounds.
scopes.lifting: Hierarchical path IDs with arbitrary subtree enumeration.

scopes.title: Sweep enumeration micro-stage
scopes.bound: SweepEnumerate(root) collects candidates = rows under root whose file is missing, snapshotting current generation per candidate, in one step; the root's candidates are added to the batch accumulated from the other roots' submissions (paths are root-disjoint, so one path-keyed batch holds them); chunking/cancel are abstracted.
scopes.why_safe: Enumeration only reads, and accumulation mirrors the code: sweep_stale_asset_paths submits one WriteOp::SweepRemoveBatch per chunk of ≤200 survivors to the writer queue, so submissions queue up rather than replacing each other. The sweep stage is entered only from the scan job's walk (single active job; no standalone trigger). The per-candidate re-check happens in SweepRecheck, so an interleaving between enumerate and re-check is modeled rather than hidden.
scopes.lifting: Chunked cancel/shutdown and per-chunk candidate re-check (sweep_stale_asset_paths chunks).

scopes.title: Sweep re-check micro-stage
scopes.bound: SweepRecheck re-checks the accumulated batch (all queued per-root submissions), dropping candidates whose generation moved, whose path is now leased, or whose file reappeared; survivors stay in sweepBatch. The re-check is per candidate and independent of the enumerating root.
scopes.why_safe: Matches sweep_stale_asset_paths inline re-checks (generation, is_busy, path.exists) performed in the sweep actor before submit; sweep_remove_batch checks only path.exists skip + asset-id/record resolution (no generation/lease re-check).
scopes.lifting: Per-chunk cancel/shutdown and interleaving between re-check and sweep_remove_batch apply (absorbed window).

scopes.title: Move lease window micro-stage
scopes.bound: ApiMoveFsOnly acquires a path lease (bumping generation) and holds it until MoveRowRewrite rewrites the row and releases it; the FS-moved/row-stale window is now visible.
scopes.why_safe: Matches lease_paths/release_generation across the FS rename to DB rewrite; generation bumps guard concurrent scans/sweeps.
scopes.lifting: Crash between FS move and row rewrite heals via sweep/backstop (SCOPE-6).

scopes.title: sweep_remove_batch micro-stage
scopes.bound: SweepRemoveBatchApply drains the accumulated re-checked batch (one writer submission per chunk of ≤200 survivors, applied per path), pruning a candidate only if its file is still absent (exists-skip) and its row still resolves (row exists); no generation or lease check.
scopes.why_safe: Matches flush_tree.rs::sweep_remove_batch exact-path resolution (path.exists skip + asset id/record resolve); prune-only.
scopes.lifting: Two-stage chain: sweep_stale_asset_paths (enumerate + inline re-checks) -> writer::submit(WriteOp::SweepRemoveBatch) -> flush_tree.rs::sweep_remove_batch (exists-skip + resolve + prune).

scopes.title: Nondeterministic scheduling
scopes.bound: Within a phase, any action classified for that phase may fire per tick: FS event, API call, fault, pipeline step, or Skip; no fairness and no ordering constraints inside a phase. The completion phases are the only sequencing: free (every environment and pipeline branch, untracked scans included, no faults), draining (work-consuming branches, at most one budgeted fault, untracked scans, then BeginScan at quiescence), scanning (one tracked CompleteScan per root, then work-consuming branches, no faults) — see stepCompletion in utils/quint/pipeline/merged.qnt. A drain fault restarts the machine in the free phase (unclean restart: requests resume and the drain is retried) and the fault budget (faults < K, K=1) bounds crash churn per attempt, so the heal cycle between faults runs uninterrupted. The phases encode the G1/G2 observation premise (changes stopped and a tracked scan completed), not pipeline inter-locking.
scopes.why_safe: The checked properties are settled-state safety properties, so scheduling nondeterminism only widens the reachable set. The request phase needs no fault branches: a crash there clears only volatile state (intake, sweep batch, path leases) that the heal scan regenerates, while durable rows and filesystem bytes survive; the one observable difference is dropped generation bumps, which moves work between queued and scan-rediscovered, and the claim already admits the scan rediscovery. The phase machine narrows the observation window deliberately: the invariant is claimed only at phase-2 quiescence, after the tracked scan of each root has drained. API calls are environment events like FS events, and the model's inter-locking is exactly the code's (generations, path leases, same-txn writes): each action models the atomicity the code provides, adds no coordination, and strips no existing lock.
scopes.lifting: Fairness-aware scheduling (alongside SCOPE-3) for liveness properties; a fault budget above one per attempt.
